I now tested it with some other variables and the task which depends on the dependencies inherit variables other than `ansible_user` also.
can you confirm #69040 fixes this issue for you?
@bcoca it looks like it should. But I have no way of testing right now...

"Reusable roles" they said :(
Any chance it gets fixed?
working on it, but there is a hard balance between getting roles working 'as they should' and not breaking existing playbooks.
sounds like it is the case, this is why people are asking for a python API instead of YAML

note: this is expected in the current implementation of roles, my 'fix' above breaks backwards compatibility and will probably not be merged w/o a toggle or a 'roles 2.0' roll out.

@tribbloid an API would have the same issue as this is built into roles and how they are loaded, unless you redefine roles, in which case ... why do you need our API?

review_comments: I see the comment below that the duplicate below needs to be removed for this to have effect, but I don't understand what the precedence change will be fixing. Role `params` having higher precedence than `include_vars` matches the docs https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/user_guide/playbooks_variables.html#variable-precedence-where-should-i-put-a-variable.
yes, that is why i made the change, but it is effectively different than what happens now
Isn't it different from the docs now that you removed it? It seemed closer to the docs before.

the big difference is that the precedence inside role stays the same but that the 'vars:'  and include_params are not exported as the 'vars/main.yml' is  so the 'general' precedence is affected since they are 'not in scope' outside the role.
Is it difficult to add test coverage for that? The several test suites modified pass without the precedence change too.
yep, that should be my next step

Could this have precedence over the _public FA default? I'm wondering if `load`/`__init__` should have public=False. This seems like it could be a breaking change potentially, like here https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.13/lib/ansible/playbook/role/__init__.py#L426 if public is not passed.
not sure, but it should be the default as that is current behaviour of `roles:` and `dependency` .. i do expect that include_role/import_role has precedence over this, but need to test
